extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of philosophy of science / metaphysics
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and explicating the philosophical principles about matter, motion, space, time, and force as presented in a philosophical/textbook chapter. Focus is on epistemological and metaphysical postulates that ground physical science (e.g., indestructibility of matter, continuity of motion, primacy of force).

rubrics_metrics.name: Force as ultimate datum of consciousness
rubrics_metrics.description: We come down then finally to Force, as the ultimate of ultimates. ... all other modes of consciousness are derivable from experiences of Force; but experiences of Force are not derivable from anything else.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Force is presented as the primordial element from which Space, Time, Matter, and Motion are built by cognition. The chapter argues that single impressions of force supply the materials for relations (thought) and that deeper modes of consciousness are traceable to experiences of force. (No explicit scoring; meant as a foundational metaphysical postulate.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Space, Time, Matter, and Motion are derived from experiences of force
rubrics_metrics.description: Space and Time, as we know them, are disclosed along with these different manifestations of Force. Matter and Motion, as we know them, are differently conditioned manifestations of Force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text repeatedly treats Space and Time as 'abstracts of the forms of relations' and Matter and Motion as 'concretes built up from the contents of various mental relations' all elaborated from impressions of force; examples include muscular tensions giving rise to concepts of position and motion. Use this criterion when assessing explanations of physical concepts: they should acknowledge their derivation from experiential impressions of force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relativity of our cognition and the unknowable Absolute
rubrics_metrics.description: Such being our cognition of the relative reality, what are we to say of the absolute reality? We can only say that it is some mode of the Unknowable, related to the Matter we know as cause to effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chapter emphasizes that our scientific/mental conceptions are relative representations of some absolute (the 'Unknowable'). When evaluating philosophical claims, require that they distinguish relative empirical concepts from claims about absolute reality and avoid conflating phenomenological data with noumenal assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific hypotheses must harmonize with universal forms (legitimacy of atomic/ether hypotheses)
rubrics_metrics.description: The atomic hypothesis, as well as the kindred hypothesis of an all-pervading ether consisting of molecules, is simply a necessary development of those universal forms which the actions of the Unknowable have wrought in us. The conclusions logically worked out by the aid of these hypotheses, are sore to be in harmony with all others which these same forms involve, and will have a relative truth that is equally complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hypotheses (e.g., atoms, ether) are legitimate as developments of cognitive forms; their value is relative and judged by logical harmony with other results and forms. Examples: atomic/ether hypotheses are accepted because they develop from universal cognitive forms and yield conclusions consistent with other knowledge. Avoid treating provisional hypotheses as absolute truths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indestructibility of Matter (empirical induction and a priori necessity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The indestructibility of Matter is proved experimentally to be an absolute uniformity within the range of our experience. ... the indestructibility of Matter thus becomes an a priori cognition of the highest order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twofold warrant: (1) empirical evidence from chemistry, weighing, combustion, evaporation, etc., shows matter is conserved in transformations; (2) psychologically/epistemologically, thought cannot represent something becoming nothing, making indestructibility an a priori presupposition of intelligible experience. Examples cited: candle combustion (carbonic acid and water weights), crystals/precipitates, comets and clouds. Anti-pattern: accepting 'creation out of nothing' without distinguishing symbolic from literal conceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indestructibility of Matter means constancy of its manifested force (resistance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Thus then by the indestructibility of Matter, we really mean the indestructibility of the force with which Matter affects us. ... we become conscious of Matter only through that resistance which it opposes to our muscular energy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationally, the permanence of matter is measured by the permanence of its force-manifestations (gravitative, chemical resistance). Examples: weighing a piece of gold before and after working it; inferring continued existence from repeated impressions (shaking hands, tactual marks). Evaluate claims about matter by whether they account for persistent force-effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity (indestructibility) of Motion
rubrics_metrics.description: The continuity of Motion, like the indestructibility of Matter, is clearly a proposition on the truth of which depends the possibility of exact Science. ... Motion, like Matter, is indestructible; whatever is lost by any one portion of matter is transferred to other portions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motion is treated as conserved (cannot be created or annihilated) and as essential for scientific explanation. Historical support: planetary motion constancy, Hooke's experiments (tops), phenomena explained by transfer of motion rather than annihilation. Use this when judging physical explanations: they should account for apparent losses of motion as transfers or transformations into imperceptible forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity of Motion as a necessity of thought (pseudo-ideas of creation/annihilation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Its destructibility never having been truly conceived at all, but having always been ... a pseudo-idea. ... The very nature of intelligence negatives the supposition that Motion can be conceived ... to either commence or cease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophically, conceiving motion to begin from nothing or lapse into nothing is impossible because thought requires relations between terms present to consciousness. When evaluating metaphysical claims about motion, require that they be representable in thought (avoid pseudo-ideas that are only symbolic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific inferences about persistence/identity rely on force-impressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever we infer the continued existence of an object, the assertion amounts to this — that an object which in past time wrought on his consciousness a certain group of changes, still exists because a like group of changes has been again wrought on his consciousness. ... the obvious postulate is, that the quantity of Matter is finally determinable by the quantity of gravitative force it manifests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identity and persistence are judged by repeatable force-effects (visual/tactual impressions, weight). Examples: eyewitness identity (handshake, missing finger), weighing transformed substances (gases after combustion). Assess observational claims by the consistency of force-impressions over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceptual/experimental examples confirming conservation (combustion, evaporation, gaseous products, planetary/ acoustic propagation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cases that once gave apparent support to the illusion that something could come out of nothing, a wider knowledge has one by one cancelled. ... the candle that had slowly burnt away, it was shown that certain calculable quantities of carbonic acid and water had resulted. ... sound propagation: impressions on the ear imply force correlatives communicated through air.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete experimental examples cited to ground abstract claims: chemical analysis balances mass (candle example); motions persist in transformed forms (sound vibrations traveling far; planetary motion inferred quantitatively). These examples are used as methodological models for claiming conservation and for making inferences from effects to causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit of scientific explanation: an inscrutable ultimate (the Unknowable / unknown symbol)
rubrics_metrics.description: If, to use an algebraic illustration, we represent Matter, Motion, and Force, by the symbols x, y, and z; then, we may ascertain the values of x and y in terms of z; but the value of z can never be found: z is the unknown quantity which must for ever remain unknown ... we have reached that limit which eternally divides science from nescience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chapter advises humility about ultimate causes: science can reduce phenomena to functions of an ultimate cause but cannot disclose that ultimate itself. When evaluating philosophical or scientific claims, recognize and mark the boundary between relative explanatory success and claims about the absolute/unconditioned.
